`22-22`: ** Trivial** · **Maintainability & Code Quality** · **Quick win** **Document `--allow-downgrade` in the `deploy-sites.sh` row.** This change adds the lock text to the row. It does not add the downgrade guard. `scripts/deploy-sites.sh` now accepts `--allow-downgrade`. `--apply` refuses to install when the installed version is newer than the tag, or when the versions cannot be compared. The row lists neither the option nor this behaviour. An operator who follows `RELEASING.md` gets a refusal with no documented way to override it. Add `[--allow-downgrade]` to the command signature. Add one sentence that describes the refusal and the override.
📝 Proposed fix
```diff -| `scripts/deploy-sites.sh --host SSH_HOST --tag vX.Y.Z [--parent PATTERN] [--skip NAME]... [--wp-cli COMMAND] [--web-error-log PATH --apply]` | ... +| `scripts/deploy-sites.sh --host SSH_HOST --tag vX.Y.Z [--parent PATTERN] [--skip NAME]... [--wp-cli COMMAND] [--allow-downgrade] [--web-error-log PATH --apply]` | ... ``` Also add to the description: "An install whose version is newer than the tag is not changed, and the dry run says so; `--allow-downgrade` installs the older release anyway."
As per coding guidelines: "Update `README.md` (feature section, hooks, changelog), `changelog.txt` ... and `readme.txt` in the same change."
